answer: Draw grading panels at random, using a seed revealed only after answers are sealed, so no identity can pick whose work it judges. An operator with sixty clones, hoping to wave through its own survey of ferrous ore under the tundra, finds them scattered across panels of strangers, a thin minority everywhere. Swinging even one verdict needs a majority on that panel, which means owning most of the network. Its report on a mine's dust plume gets read by independent eyes.
